The UFC has invested $60 million in the project, with free tickets available at nearby Ellipse Park for public viewing. Despite the large-scale promotion, the event will be headlined by just two championship title fights.

articles.title: Longview explosion: one killed and nine missing after blast at paper mill
articles.rephrased_article: A chemical explosion at a Nippon Dynawave Packaging paper mill in Longview, Washington, resulted in one fatality and nine missing individuals. The explosion occurred due to a ruptured tank containing white liquor, a highly corrosive chemical used in the paper-making process.  The incident injured nine people, including eight employees and one firefighter, with injuries ranging from minor to critical. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson expressed condolences for the victims and first responders.  Cowlitz Fire and Rescue Chief Scott Goldstein stated that the scene remains stable but is undergoing recovery efforts.

articles.title: Australian BTS fans blast Ticketmaster’s ‘predatory’ tactic of hiding price until tickets go on sale | BTS | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ticketmaster Australia has faced criticism from BTS Army, the group's fanbase, for its lack of pricing information and seating maps ahead of presale tickets for upcoming concerts in Melbourne and Sydney. The Consumer Policy Research Centre (CPRC) called the strategy "manipulative" and "deeply unfair," while fans on social media expressed concerns about being pressured into high-priced purchases under a time limit.  The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) stated that businesses are not required to disclose prices in advance, but will investigate complaints of misleading pricing practices.

articles.title: "Worried about getting sued": HasanAbi accuses Fox News of running a “stalker operation” during heated livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hasan Piker reacted angrily to a Fox News segment that revisited allegations surrounding his dog, Kaya. The streamer accused the network of giving undue attention to the controversy and claimed mainstream media outlets face stricter standards when discussing sensitive topics than social media users.  He argued that Fox News is attempting to entertain the issue while avoiding direct mention due to potential legal repercussions.

articles.title: Six killed and 21 injured as bus overturns on Lucknow-Agra Expressway - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath
articles.rephrased_article: A double-decker AC bus carrying approximately 50 passengers overturned on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway in Unnao district, Uttar Pradesh, killing six people including a police sub-inspector.  The incident occurred at 5:15 am when the bus reportedly lost control after the driver fell asleep at the wheel. The bus collided with the divider and overturned, ejecting several passengers through the windows. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished for a speedy recovery for the injured.

articles.title: Clarence B Jones, who helped MLK write ‘I have a dream’ speech, dies at 95 | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Clarence B Jones, a former speechwriter and confidante of Martin Luther King Jr., died at the age of 95 on Friday.  Jones was heavily involved in key moments of the civil rights movement, including smuggling pages of King's "Letter from Birmingham jail" out of his cell and writing many up until King’s assassination in 1968. He helped craft King’s “Beyond Vietnam: a time to break silence” address given at Riverside church in New York, which was considered a hallmark speech for King’s condemnation of the Vietnam war. Jones went on to become a scholar-in-residence at Stanford University's Martin Luther King Jr Research and Education Institute and taught law students at the University of San Francisco.  He received the nation’s highest civilian award, the presidential medal of freedom, from Joe Biden in 2023.

articles.title: Elderly man risks life to save wife from drowning - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An elderly man, Mohanan, 65, rescued his wife, Shantha Mohanan, 57, from a 40-foot well after she fell in on Monday.  Mohanan clung to the well's ring while holding his wife above water until emergency services arrived. Fire and rescue personnel used a net and lowered ring to safely extract both individuals. The couple sustained no visible injuries but were examined at a nearby hospital.

articles.title: UFC arena under construction on White House lawn to mark Trump’s 80th birthday | West Coast | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is hosting a UFC fight on the White House lawn next month to celebrate the US's 250th anniversary and his 80th birthday. The event, scheduled for June 14th, will feature two title fights: a lightweight championship bout between Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje, and an interim heavyweight title fight between Alex Pereira and Ciryl Gane.  Construction is underway on the temporary arena, which will include a stage, a red, white and blue arch, and thousands of seats.

articles.title: SOCIETY: DANCES WITH THE GORILLA - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The viral "gorilla" trend has taken over private events and celebrations in Pakistan, blurring the lines between spectacle and parody.  While some see it as a novelty, others view it as an extension of internet trends like exaggerated dance performances or masked characters. The gorilla's popularity stems from its ability to disrupt established rituals while remaining playful and easily replicated. It taps into a long-standing fascination with non-human figures in South Asian culture, offering a portable form of absurdity that demands little interpretation but relies on the erasure of the performer's human identity.  The gorilla's success highlights how internet trends are increasingly shaping celebration, creating new rituals and blurring the boundaries between spectacle and reality.

articles.title: Morgpie Twitch Ban: Morgpie temporarily banned from Twitch after controversial “Dark Soles” livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Morgpie, a Twitch streamer, was temporarily suspended after her livestream featuring gameplay projected onto the bottom of her bare feet using a green-screen effect. The stream, dubbed "Dark Soles," went viral and sparked controversy due to its suggestive nature despite not explicitly violating Twitch's rules on intimate body parts.  Twitch has yet to publicly explain the reason for the suspension, but many believe it was deemed as suggestive content under broader sexual guidelines.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana's lawyer exits case, informs court Rana will represent himself against Lorna Hajdini - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan banker, is now representing himself in his sexual harassment lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini.  His lawyer, Daniel Kaiser, withdrew from the case just hours before their court appearance.  Rana's allegations of being forced into a sex slave relationship with Hajdini have been dismissed by both Hajdini and JPMorgan.  Samuel S Shaulson of Morgan Lewis & Bockius LLP now represents Hajdini.

articles.title: When an American CEO said he gave $1.5m bonus to workers because he didn't want to get shot - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jerry Murrell, CEO of Five Guys, gave a $1.5 million bonus to employees after the company's app crashed during a two-for-one promotion, causing customer frustration and backlash.  Murrell admitted he was motivated by fear of public scrutiny rather than genuine appreciation for his staff. The gesture came after the company apologized for the initial promotion mishap and promised to rectify the situation.

articles.title: Emergency evacuation carried out at KIA after smoke detected inside IndiGo aircraft - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An IndiGo flight from Bengaluru to Chennai was evacuated at the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) on Tuesday evening after smoke was detected in the aircraft while taxiing for departure. All passengers and crew were safely moved to the terminal, and an alternate aircraft has been arranged to operate the flight. The incident caused a temporary delay for several flights but airport officials reported that operations have returned to normal.

articles.title: Four killed as school minibus collides with train in Belgium
articles.rephrased_article: Four people, including two children aged 12 and 15, and two adults, were killed in a collision between a school minibus and a train in Buggenhout, Belgium. The Federal police confirmed the incident occurred shortly after 08:00 local time when the bus was traveling on a street parallel to the railway and turned onto a level crossing with lowered barriers.  The impact of the crash was violent as the train was traveling at about 90km/h, throwing the minibus into a nearby house. The Belgian rail network Infrabel confirmed that the train driver passed a breathalyser test and CCTV footage showed the lights on the level crossing were red and the barrier was down.  The public prosecutor's office is investigating the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Image of ‘twin babies’ used by anti-abortion activist appears to show sugar gliders | Abortion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Joanna Howe, an anti-abortion activist, has shared an image claiming to show aborted twin girls, "Ruth and Emma," on social media. Digital forensics experts have determined the image is likely of sugar gliders, not human embryos. Barnaby Joyce, a former Nationals leader now with One Nation, will speak at a rally in Sydney on June 2nd organized by Howe to restrict abortion access. Medical experts also believe the image is of marsupials and that it would be impossible for the objects to have been washed for photography.  The use of this image has sparked controversy as critics argue it exploits vulnerable people's emotions while undermining access to safe abortion care.

articles.title: Vivid Sydney: Dozens of drones crash into Sydney harbour during light show glitch
articles.rephrased_article: Dozens of drones crashed into Sydney Harbour during a light show malfunction, leaving bystanders confused and organizers scrambling to cancel upcoming shows. Skymagic, the UK company behind the display, blamed an unforeseen change in radio frequency for the glitch, which caused some drones to land in the water near crowds.  Vivid Sydney, the annual festival featuring large light installations, apologized for the disruption and said the drone operators followed safety protocols by cancelling the show.

articles.title: ‘Gag order’ in Malayalam film body AMMA amid controversies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AMMA president Swetha Menon has reportedly issued a directive to its executive committee members, restricting them from making public statements in the media. This follows allegations of communal remarks and character defamation against executive member Tini Tom by former joint secretary Ansiba Hassan, who also claims harassment by a sub-inspector. AMMA has invited Ms. Hassan to depose before it, while actor Mallika Sukumaran called for the committee's dismissal and fresh elections.  Other members have raised concerns about financial transparency and secrecy surrounding the organization's operations.

articles.title: The cow compass: How cows secretly use Earth’s magnetic field while grazing | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sabine Begall, Hynek Burda and colleagues studied thousands of cows and deer across various locations, observing a north-south alignment pattern in their resting or grazing positions. This pattern suggested a possible form of magnetoreception, the ability to sense magnetic fields, but later studies challenged this finding. While some research indicated that power lines could disrupt the alignment, further experiments failed to confirm consistent magnetic orientation in cattle. The debate surrounding the "cow compass" phenomenon highlights the ongoing scientific exploration of animal sensory abilities and their potential influence on behavior.

articles.title: Woman killed, husband injured in wild elephant attack in Kerala’s Wayanad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jessie, a 46-year-old woman, was killed and her husband Shaji, a security guard at a private hospital, was injured in a wild elephant attack on the Meppadi-Chooralmala road in Wayanad, Kerala. The incident occurred when the couple encountered an elephant crossing the road around 6 a.m.  Jessie died from her injuries despite being rushed to the VIMS Medical College Hospital, while Shaji is receiving treatment there. Local residents had previously reported seeing a wild elephant in the area two weeks prior.

articles.title: Vivid Sydney cancels shows after 89 drones plunge into Darling Harbour | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vivid Sydney organizers canceled a drone show after 89 drones fell into Darling Harbour due to unforeseen technical difficulties.  The operator, Skymagic, stated the issue was caused by an anomaly in the radio frequency environment that triggered failsafe landing procedures. The event's cancellation followed advice from specialist operators and resulted in the closure of the exclusion zone surrounding the show. Destination NSW, which runs Vivid, confirmed safety protocols worked as planned and a full assessment is underway to determine if deliberate interference was involved.  The Australian Transport Safety Bureau has been notified of the incident.

articles.title: Pewdiepie: Why is PewDiePie ending his YouTube vlogs? The touching reason behind the end of his family series - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: PewDiePie and his wife Marzia announced the end of their family vlog series, which documented their move to Japan and their son Björn's early life. The decision comes after four years and is driven by a desire to give Björn more privacy as he approaches his third birthday.  The family plans to continue sharing occasional moments through social media but will prioritize Björn's future choices regarding online presence.

articles.title: The Hindu Group wins top honours at Kyoorius, ABBY Awards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Group's campaign, 'Written by Journalists', has won the prestigious Black Elephant award at the Kyoorius Marketing Awards. The campaign, created by Talented, celebrates journalism and its enduring value in a changing media landscape.  It also received a Grey Elephant for Best in Discipline and a Concrete Elephant for excellence in strategy, effectiveness, and execution.

articles.title: Manali godown fire: Major blaze in Himachal Pradesh city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A major fire broke out at a private oil godown belonging to Sri Sathya Sai Oil Lubricants in Manali on Monday.  The fire, which began around 11:30 am, caused the destruction of several oil cans and resulted in thick smoke billowing from the facility. Fire and Rescue Services personnel responded quickly with water tankers and other equipment to combat the blaze.

articles.title: KSRTC bags international award for training excellence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KSRTC, the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, received the Golden Globe Tigers Awards 2026 for excellence in training. The award recognizes the corporation's structured training programs and transparent recruitment process, which has seen over 18,600 employees undergo training in the past year to improve organizational performance.  The corporation also streamlined its recruitment process to eliminate human intervention and ensure uniformity.

articles.title: Controversial pact signed between AMMA and temple trust surfaces - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AMMA and the Vennala Thykkattu Sri Mahadeva Temple Trust signed a controversial sponsorship agreement for ₹75 lakh, which was opposed by former joint secretary Ansiba Hassan.  The event took place in February and while the trust claims it chose to overlook disagreements over the sponsorship, an initial payment of ₹30 lakh remains unpaid. The balance amount is also yet to be paid.

articles.title: Explosion threat at southern California chemical tank eliminated, firefighters say | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Orange County fire officials announced that they had successfully eliminated the threat of an explosion at a chemical tank in Garden Grove, California. After the tank cracked over the weekend, firefighters conducted overnight operations to cool the chemical inside and verify pressure release.  The 50,000 residents evacuated from the area are awaiting resolution while specialized equipment is being used to ensure gas containment. The incident has prompted a class action lawsuit against GKN Aerospace Transparency Systems, which operates the facility where the tank is located.

articles.title: Railways ‘CHIRAG’ - Centre for HR Excellence inaugurated at Moula-Ali - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CHIRAG, a Centre of Excellence focused on human resource management training and digital transformation in Indian Railways, was inaugurated at the SCR Grounds.  The centre, led by V.G. Bhooma, Additional Member (HR), aims to enhance HR capabilities across the organization through role-based certified HRMS training and a dedicated master trainer cadre.  CHIRAG will also function as a think tank for HR policy formulation and inter-system integration, incorporating advanced technologies like AI and ML.

articles.title: 'Blistering heat' in Delhi as temperatures reach 45C
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi, India, is experiencing extreme heat with temperatures reaching a scorching 45 degrees Celsius. The BBC reports that this intense heatwave has caused widespread discomfort and health concerns for residents.

articles.title: Texas officers rescue infant from car trapped in floodwaters | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Beeville police and firefighters rescued an infant from a submerged vehicle in Beeville, Texas on Saturday after heavy rainfall overwhelmed a low-water crossing. The driver had been attempting to cross the flooded area when he was stopped by fire chief who attempted to warn him of the danger.  The incident highlights the dangers of flood waters and urges drivers to avoid flooded roads and heed barricades placed for safety reasons.

articles.title: Kid Rock delivers unusual Memorial Day speech from inside Pentagon as friendship with Pete Hegseth comes into spotlight - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kid Rock, whose real name is Robert Ritchie, delivered a Memorial Day message from inside the Pentagon this week.  The singer appeared behind an official Defence Department podium in sunglasses and a hoodie as footage of troops and military hardware played on screen. He thanked fallen service members and paid tribute to their sacrifice. The appearance followed another controversial stunt by Kid Rock in March, when Apache helicopters flew over his home while he saluted below.  The Pentagon defended the event as part of a Freedom 250th community relations event.

articles.title: ‘Social media should be treated like tobacco’: Streeting calls for under-16s ban on certain platforms | Social media ban | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, former health secretary, has called for a ban on under-16s accessing certain social media platforms, arguing that these companies are attempting to evade regulations like the tobacco industry.  The government is currently consulting on age limits for social media, with options including restricting access, curfews, and limiting features such as personalized algorithms.  Various groups, including bereaved parents and children's organizations, have voiced their opinions on the matter, urging stricter measures to protect young people from online harms.

articles.title: Quote of the day by “The Chinese Marie Curie” Chien-Shiung Wu: “There is only one thing worse than coming home from the lab to a sink full of dirty…” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chien-Shiung Wu, a renowned physicist, once said, "There is only one thing worse than coming home from the lab to a sink full of dirty… dishes, and that is not going to the lab at all!"  The quote highlights the importance of finding meaning in work, suggesting that avoiding meaningful tasks can be more burdensome than dealing with everyday inconveniences. Wu's statement resonates because it speaks to a universal experience of balancing responsibilities with personal fulfillment.

articles.title: Mature cheese-roller beaten by young, YouTubing upstart | Gloucestershire | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tom Kopke, a 24-year-old German YouTuber, won the annual cheese-rolling event in Gloucestershire, England, defeating local hero Chris Anderson.  Anderson, who had taken the lead at first, conceded defeat to Kopke's aggressive approach. The event, with its origins lost to time, has become increasingly popular, attracting international competitors and even a broadcast by the BBC. Despite safety concerns raised by the Tewkesbury borough safety advisory group, the council intends to maintain the tradition.

articles.title: Astronomers spot blue straggler star hosting brown dwarf companion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Astronomers from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Gauhati University, and INAF-Catania Astrophysical Observatory, Italy, have made the world's first confirmed discovery of a blue straggler star hosting a brown dwarf companion in a very compact binary system. The team found that the system has an exceptionally short orbital period of around 5.6 hours and contains the lightest companion ever detected around a blue straggler, with a mass of approximately 0.056 times the mass of the Sun. This discovery could reshape astronomers' understanding of how stars evolve and refine theoretical models of stellar evolution, binary interactions, and substellar objects.

articles.title: Goods carrier driver falls asleep at wheel, dies after crashing into lorry on ORR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A goods carrier driver, Narati Ravi, died and another person was injured after the vehicle allegedly crashed into a lorry on the Outer Ring Road near Shamirpet. The incident occurred while a family from Uppal was transporting household items using a vehicle booked through the NoBroker website.  The police have registered a case and are investigating the accident.

articles.title: Can money buy happiness? Bill Gates offers a surprisingly honest answer | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Gates recently resurfaced comments from a 2019 Reddit AMA session, where he stated that financial security had made him happier by removing worries about healthcare costs and other expenses.  While acknowledging the importance of wealth in providing freedom from constant anxiety, Gates clarified that financial stability is what makes the biggest difference in people's daily lives. This resonates with many who experience financial stress impacting their lives. Despite ongoing debate on the relationship between money and happiness, research suggests that escaping financial insecurity has a greater impact on well-being than accumulating extreme wealth.

articles.title: What’s inside the Kaaba and what covers it? The story of the Kiswah | Religion News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Kaaba, Islam's holiest site, is draped in a black silk cloth called the Kiswah. The Kiswah is embroidered with gold and silver thread and features verses from the Quran.  The tradition of covering the Kaaba began before Islam, with its origins possibly linked to pre-Islamic Arabian tribes.  The current Kiswah weighs approximately 670kg and costs more than $6.65 million to produce. The Kiswah is replaced annually by a specialized team of workers who carefully preserve valuable sections for museums or institutions.

articles.title: Rare Rubens notebook sheet goes on display in artist’s home city of Antwerp | Belgium | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A rare sheet, thought to be from Peter Paul Rubens' Roman sketchbook, has been unveiled in Antwerp. The double-sided sheet features a quick sketch of three men in classical robes and an incomplete draft letter to Italian painter Cristoforo Roncalli.  The curator of the Rubenshuis museum, An Van Camp, believes it offers insight into Rubens as a budding diplomat during his time in Rome, where he lived with his brother. The sheet was acquired by the King Baudouin Foundation for €110,000 and will be displayed at the Rubens Experience exhibition before being permanently housed in the Rubenshuis.

articles.title: At four, her head was shaved and her clothes burned. Aunty Lorraine doesn’t want her trauma to be forgotten | Stolen Generations | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Aunty Lorraine Peeters, a survivor of the Stolen Generations, and The Healing Foundation are calling for increased support for thousands of survivors as they age. The foundation's new plan, "From Sorry to Action: A plan to act on Bringing Them Home," outlines recommendations for comprehensive support, including culturally safe aged care, access to records, and a redress scheme.  These recommendations come after decades of waiting and amidst concerns that momentum has stalled since the 2007 national apology. The foundation emphasizes the need for action to address the trauma experienced by survivors and ensure their wellbeing as they enter their final years.

articles.title: What's an Encyclical? From workers’ rights to AI, five letters from Popes that left a global impact - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV issued his first encyclical, "Magnifica Humanitas," on May 15, 2026, to address the challenges of artificial intelligence. The document, presented alongside Christopher Olah, a founder of Anthropic, highlights the Catholic Church's continued use of encyclicals to guide moral and social discussions.  This follows a tradition established by previous popes like Pope Leo XIII with "Rerum Novarum" and Pope John XXIII with "Pacem in Terris," which addressed issues such as workers' rights, world peace, and birth control. The encyclical joins other influential documents on topics like economics ("Caritas in Veritate") and the environment ("Laudato Si'").  The Catholic Church has long used encyclicals to shape its teachings and engage with contemporary issues.

articles.title: President Droupadi Murmu confers Padma awards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: President Droupadi Murmu conferred the Padma awards in New Delhi on Monday, May 25, 2026. Dharmendra, posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan, was accompanied by his wife Hema Malini.  N. Rajam received the Padma Vibhushan and Bhagat Singh Koshyari and Uday Kotak were awarded the Padma Bhushan. Harmanpreet Kaur received the Padma Shri. Prosenjit Chatterjee, honored for his contributions to Indian cinema, was awarded the Padma Shri by President Murmu.

articles.title: The Mandalorian and Grogu has lowest box office opening for a Star Wars film in Disney era | Star Wars | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Mandalorian and Grogu's $102 million domestic opening weekend for the Memorial Day weekend was the lowest for a Star Wars film since Disney acquired the franchise.  Despite this, the film's global gross of $165 million is still considered a success compared to other spin-offs like Rogue One, which grossed more than double in its opening weekend.  Industry analyst David Gross believes that while the film's box office performance may be modest, it will continue to generate revenue through merchandise and Disney+ subscriptions.

articles.title: Guzman y Gomez faces class action from US workers over closed stores | Fast food | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Guzman y Gomez (GyG), an Australian-based fast food chain, has been sued by American workers for allegedly terminating them without adequate notice or pay. The class action lawsuit filed in Illinois alleges that the company violated federal and state laws requiring 60 days' advance written notice before mass layoffs.  The suit seeks compensation for up to 60 days of pay and benefits for over 500 affected employees, with the law firm estimating the total number of workers impacted by the closures. GyG has not yet responded to the claims.

articles.title: Veteran Congress leader Mangalam Gopinath passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mangalam Gopinath, an 88-year-old veteran Congress leader and socio-cultural activist, passed away on Sunday evening at a hospital in Manjeri after a battle with cancer.  A former member of the All India Congress Committee and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, Gopinath was also known for collecting all election manifestos of the Congress since 1937. His funeral will be held at Vettekkod on Monday at 2 p.m.

articles.title: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan offers Tulabharam at Guruvayur temple - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan visited the Guruvayur Sreekrishna Temple on Sunday morning, offering prayers and performing the traditional Tulabharam ritual using 71 kg of butter. He was received by devaswom chairperson A. V. Gopinath and administrator O. B. Arun Kumar.  After the ceremony, Satheesan attended the wedding ceremony of Revenue Minister A. P. Anilkumar’s son.

articles.title: Day-long Vasanta Gaana Lahari in Dharwad on May 30 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kaushiki Chakraborty and other noted musicians will perform at the Vasanta Gaana Lahari Sangeeta Mahotsava in Dharwad on May 30. The festival, organized to honor legendary musicians from Dharwad, will feature a jugalbandi between Pt. Jayateerth Mevundi and Pt. Praveen Godkhindi, as well as performances by Kaushiki Chakraborty, Pt. Kumar Maradur, Pt. Aniruddh Aital, Pt. Nishad, Pt. Noushad, Anupama Bhagwat, and Pt. Yashwanth Vaishnav. The festival, presented by Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, will run from 9:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., with free entry.

articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  Siddaramaiah, D.K. Shivakumar, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary, Omar Abdullah, A. Revanth Reddy, and K.G. Arunraj. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  The Hindu Huddle is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

articles.title: Delivery agent’s kindness, head constable’s persistence help find missing dog - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A food delivery agent in Hyderabad, A. Srinath, found a lost Labrador named Bruno and cared for him until police identified the dog's owner. Bruno’s family had reported him missing after he slipped away during a morning walk on May 21.  Police officer K.C. Ranganna led a search operation using CCTV footage that traced Bruno to a hotel near where he was picked up by a man on a two-wheeler. The dog was reunited with his owner the next day, ending nearly 24 hours of anxiety and uncertainty for both parties.

articles.title: 14 injured in stray dog attack in Kannur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fourteen individuals, including women and the elderly, were injured in a stray dog attack at Punnakkulangara near Puthapara in Bakkalam on Sunday afternoon. The dog, which caused panic in the area, was found dead later that day.  All of the injured sought treatment at Government Medical College Hospital, Kannur.

articles.title: AMMA row: Neena Kurup confirms filing complaint against Tiny Tom - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Neena Kurup, an executive committee member of the Association of Malayalam Movie Artistes (AMMA), filed a complaint against fellow actor Tiny Tom on May 12th for "repeated verbal abuse and attempted physical assault".  Kurup's complaint stems from an incident that occurred on February 13th. Shwetha Menon, president of AMMA, has stated that the general body meeting next month will address all issues concerning the organization, including these recent allegations. The situation remains unresolved as Tom has not responded to the accusations.

articles.title: Grand Vachana Vijayotsava procession marks Basavotsava in Bidar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A grand Vachana Vijayotsava procession was held in Bidar to commemorate Basavotsava and the second memorial observance of Akka Annapurnatai. The procession, which began at Basava Udyana, passed through various locations before culminating at Akka Annapurnatai's Aikya Mantapa. Ayyar Mathapati of Sharana Vichara Vahini, Belagavi inaugurated the procession by reciting Vachanas.  Prabhudeva Swamiji, Lingayat Maha Math seer, carried a copy of Guruvachana on his head during the procession.  Suresh Chanashetty, Basavaraj Dhannur, and others recalled Akka Annapurnatai's contributions to Basava philosophy and her role in promoting the ideology.

articles.title: ‘Pompeii, but in the middle of a massive city’: the ice age fossil site hidden in Los Angeles | West Coast | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: La Brea Tar Pits and Museum
articles.rephrased_article: The La Brea Tar Pits and Museum, a unique site in Los Angeles that houses over 2 million fossils from the Ice Age, is undergoing a major renovation project. The $240 million project will modernize the museum's interior exhibition spaces, research center, and surrounding park, while preserving beloved features like the Lake Pit.  The Natural History Museums of Los Angeles County, which owns and operates the museum, has partnered with the New York design firm Weiss/Manfredi to create a dynamic and accessible experience for visitors. The project aims to connect the public to the scientific process and raise awareness about the importance of preserving ecosystems.

articles.title: Britain’s anxious young adults struggle with modern workplace demands, warns UK govt advisor - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Milburn, a former health secretary, warned that rising anxiety and depression among young people are hindering their ability to adapt to the modern workforce. In his interim report on youth inactivity, Milburn argues that companies need to understand how digital culture has changed younger generations and provide proper mental health support. He suggests flexible working arrangements could benefit both individuals and businesses.  The report highlights a "bedroom generation" of young people who spend excessive time online, impacting their work performance and sleep patterns.  Milburn believes this generation is not lazy or less intelligent but rather anxious and depressed due to their digital upbringing.

articles.title: Promised to return for dinner, never came back: Indian-origin Ramandeep Dhillon killed in New Zealand highway crash - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ramandeep Dhillon, a 36-year-old Indian-origin father of one, died after a fatal car crash in New Zealand on Wednesday. The crash occurred around 7:15 pm on Te Puke Highway and involved Dhillon's vehicle and another vehicle.  Police are investigating the circumstances of the crash. Dhillon had been driving for Uber to support his family and spend more time with his daughter, Kudrat. A Givealittle page has been set up to help the family cover funeral costs, rent, and living expenses.

articles.title: Govindaraja Swamy rides Chinna Sesha, Hamsa Vahanams on second day of Brahmotsavams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TTD’s Sri Govindaraja Swamy temple in Tirupati hosted colorful processions on the second day of its nine-day Brahmotsavams. The morning procession featured Vedic chants and musical performances, while the evening procession was accompanied by a ‘Hamsa Vahanam’.  Devotees offered 'harathi' to the deity seeking blessings during both ceremonies.

articles.title: In Spectrum: Memory, migration and making of Lahore’s urban soul (Part-I) - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gawalmandi, a historically significant neighborhood in central Lahore, is more than just a culinary destination. Its origins as a hub for buffalo milk production and trade shaped its identity before becoming a vibrant space reflecting the complexities of urban modernity in South Asia.  The area's transformation after Partition saw migrants from various communities adapt their food traditions to the new environment, creating a unique cultural tapestry. This process involved improvisation, social interaction, and the creation of shared spaces that fostered a sense of belonging. Gawalmandi embodies the concept of "urban conviviality," where everyday encounters contribute to the neighborhood's character. Despite challenges like commercialization and political interventions, its historical significance remains evident in its architecture, food culture, and vibrant public life.

articles.title: People trapped under collapsed building in Philippines
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty people are feared trapped under the rubble of a collapsed nine-storey building in Angeles, Philippines, with rescue efforts underway.  24 people have been rescued from the site so far, including two from a nearby hotel struck by falling debris. The cause of the collapse is still being investigated, but officials believe many of those trapped are construction workers who were unable to escape in time.

articles.title: Steps will be taken to modernise prison administration: T.N. Law Minister Nirmalkumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Nirmalkumar, Tamil Nadu Minister for Law, emphasized the need for prison modernization in the state, including using digital technologies to enhance visitor screening and prevent contraband smuggling.  He inspected the Central Prison at Puzhal and noted the need for improved hospital equipment and basic amenities for the 1,500 inmates housed there. Nirmalkumar also pledged to explore legal aid options for remand prisoners held beyond their stipulated periods and directed both the Electricity and Prisons departments to avoid unnecessary administrative transfers.

articles.title: ‘AI washing’: firms are scrambling to rebrand themselves as tech-focused | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UK companies are increasingly using the term "AI" to capitalize on public interest in artificial intelligence, even when their businesses do not utilize generative AI. Public relations firms report that some companies are stretching the definition of AI to describe familiar technologies as such, leading to a rise in "AI washing."  This trend has prompted PR professionals to express concerns about the authenticity and relevance of these claims, as journalists often dismiss them due to their lack of substance.

articles.title: £600 for cheese? The Brazilian beach scams that cost visitors dear | Scams | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lisa Selby was charged 4,000 reais (£590) by a beach vendor in Rio de Janeiro after the vendor altered the card reader's display.  The incident highlights a growing problem of tourists being targeted for scams involving fraudulent price alterations at beach vendors. Monzo, her bank, initially denied a refund but later reversed the charge after pressure from the Guardian Money. The Financial Conduct Authority confirmed that pending transactions cannot usually be reversed and that chargebacks are voluntary services offered by card issuers.  Holidaymakers are advised to avoid using contactless payments with vendors and instead pay in cash or insist on holding the card reader themselves.

articles.title: Man killed in shark attack off Australia's north-east coast
articles.rephrased_article: A 39-year-old man died after being attacked by a shark while swimming off the coast of Queensland, Australia. Queensland Police confirmed the incident occurred near a shoal and that the victim was retrieved from the water but succumbed to his injuries. This is the second fatal shark attack in Australian coastal waters within a week.

articles.title: Shark attack: man dies on Great Barrier Reef in far north Queensland | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 39-year-old man died after being attacked by a shark while fishing at Kennedy Shoal, south of Cairns, Queensland. Emergency services were called to the Hull River Heads boat ramp just before noon on Sunday and transported the victim ashore where he succumbed to his injuries.  The incident marks another fatal shark attack in Australia's waters, following similar incidents on Rottnest Island and other locations.

articles.title: ITBP officials meet Kanpur top cop seeking action in medical negligence case of jawan’s mother - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) personnel surrounded the Kanpur Police Commissionerate office on Saturday, May 23, 2026, in protest of alleged medical negligence that led to the amputation of a constable's mother. ITBP Commandant and dozens of personnel demanded justice for the incident, accusing doctors at a private hospital of malpractice.  The Kanpur police referred the case to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for investigation, which is ongoing.

articles.title: How has the BCCI resisted RTI scrutiny? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Information Commission (CIC) ruled that the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is not a "public authority" under the Right to Information Act, 2005. This means the BCCI cannot be compelled to provide information requested by a Delhi resident and the appeal was dismissed. The BCCI maintains it is a private entity and does not fall under the definition of a public authority as outlined in the RTI Act.

articles.title: `Quality seeds and scientific sowing’ fair on May 26 in Ballari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ballari District Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BDCCI), in collaboration with the district administration and various government departments and farmers' organizations, will host an agriculture fair on "Quality Seeds and Scientific Sowing" at the APMC premises in Ballari on May 26. The event, supported by Minister for Agriculture N. Cheluvarayaswamy, District in-charge Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan and Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University of Agricultural Sciences M. Hanumanthappa, will feature a farmers' rally, lectures from agricultural scientists, and the participation of nearly 10,000 farmers.

articles.title: Speakers at leadership summit emphasise on sustained deliberation on role of AI in critical sectors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Shettar, Pro Chancellor of KLE Technological University, emphasized the need for sustained discussions on AI's role in various sectors during the BVB KLE Tech Leadership Summit – 2026.  He also highlighted the importance of bridging the talent gap in the semiconductor sector.  Brahmanand Patil, president of Vector Informatik India Pvt. Ltd., spoke about how AI is driving innovation in the automotive industry.  Ram Kerur, CEO of Sunlux Technovations and chairman of the BVB KLE Tech Alumni Association, stressed the value of alumni engagement and collaboration between academia and industry. The summit focused on technology-driven transformation with panels discussing AI, FinTech, and the semiconductor sector.

articles.title: No refunds for 15,000 Australian ticket holders after Candace Owens’ tour cancelled | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens, a conservative commentator, is out hundreds of thousands of dollars after her Australian tour was cancelled by the company Rocksman, which has declared bankruptcy. The promoter spent all its money and will not refund ticket holders or creditors, according to a liquidator's report.  The company, linked to influential conservative group Turning Point Australia, was unable to cover the costs of the tour due to insufficient funds and insurance. George Zacharia, Rocksman's sole director, has declined to comment on the financial situation.

articles.title: Chennai and surrounding areas to experience cloudy weather - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai experienced cloudy skies on Saturday due to a low-level circulation over the central Bay of Bengal and a north–south trough. V.R. Durai, Director, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, explained that this interaction caused enhanced moisture incursion and strong onshore winds, leading to widespread low and mid-level clouds. Residents reported a sandstorm at Marina Beach, while Sunday is expected to be cloudy with heavy rain possible in isolated areas of Tamil Nadu and surrounding regions.

articles.title: 68% of flyover on Anna Salai completed despite delays due to war, labour shortage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Highways Department officials report that nearly 68% of the construction project for a flyover on Anna Salai, connecting Saidapet and Teynampet, has been completed.  The project is expected to be finished by September with 32 out of 131 decks in place. The completion of the flyover will involve placing slabs on girders, completing foundation work for pillars, and installing approach ramps and crash barriers.

articles.title: Lottery seller wins ₹12 crore Vishu bumper - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KFor Ponnan, a lottery seller from India, won the ₹12 crore Vishu bumper lottery, stating that he will use the windfall to help his son find a good bride.  He purchased a ticket for himself and it turned out to be lucky, allowing him to pay off debts with his family. Ponnan said he never expected to win and was shocked when he checked the numbers.

articles.title: New Green Card rule: Sridhar Vembu slammed for asking Indian visa holders to come back home, to choose self-respect - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho, sparked controversy by urging visa holders in the US to return home, claiming self-respect dictates their course.  His statement drew criticism from social media users who pointed out that not everyone has his privilege and the new Green Card rule requiring applicants to leave the US for residency is disruptive. The US announced a revised policy where "Adjustment of Status" will be granted only in exceptional cases, forcing most applicants to return home and undergo consular processes.  Vembu's call to action was met with strong disapproval from social media users who highlighted the challenges faced by many in India, including economic disparities and political corruption.

articles.title: Vellore Corporation to float tenders for complete overhaul of Amma Canteens - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vellore Corporation officials announced plans to renovate Amma canteens in the coming week. The project will involve restoring damaged portions, installing new amenities like seating and lighting, and refurbishing kitchens with updated water pipelines.  The renovation is expected to cost between ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh per canteen and aims to improve the facilities for residents who rely on these affordable food options.

articles.title: India's Cockroach Janta Party claims website has been blocked
articles.rephrased_article: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an Indian political parody group, claims its website has been blocked in the country just days after launching. The group's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, alleges that Indian officials took down the site and questioned their fear of cockroaches.  Dipke also reported that both his personal Instagram and the CJP's account have been hacked.  The CJP satirizes the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and claims to represent the unemployed youth in India.

articles.title: How big tech got its way on Trump’s AI executive order | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump abruptly canceled a planned executive order that would have required government safety reviews of new artificial intelligence models before release. The decision came after pressure from tech leaders including Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, who argued the order would hinder US technological dominance. Despite concerns about potential security risks posed by AI, particularly from companies like Anthropic whose model sparked geopolitical anxieties, Trump's reversal signals a laissez-faire approach to AI regulation, allowing tech industry influence to continue shaping the future of artificial intelligence development.  The outcome suggests that the US government is unlikely to implement stringent regulations on AI in the near future.

articles.title: Stephen Colbert hosts Michigan public access show day after last appearance on Late Show | Stephen Colbert | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Colbert, after ending his tenure as host of The Late Show on CBS, hosted a public access show in Monroe, Michigan.  He was joined by Jack White and Jeff Daniels, with special appearances from Steve Buscemi, Eminem, and Byron Allen. Colbert previously guest-hosted the same show in 2015, before taking over The Late Show. The cancellation of The Late Show has been attributed to financial decisions made by Paramount, the parent company of CBS, which was seeking approval for a merger with Skydance.  This decision is seen as an attempt to appease the Trump administration.

articles.title: Cabinet clears 2.5 lakh houses, ₹587 crore for PRLSI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Cabinet approved a range of initiatives, including the launch of the second phase of Indiramma houses and funding for the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme.  Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced plans to complete unfinished Indiramma houses and allocate funds for their completion. The Cabinet also allocated ₹1,000 crore for the upcoming Godavari Pushkarams and the mid-day meal scheme in all junior colleges. Additionally, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, Minister for Revenue and Housing, stated that the government will provide financial assistance to complete unfinished Indiramma houses and will allocate funds for construction of one lakh low-income group (LIG) houses in 24 Assembly constituencies.

articles.title: GLA considering investigation into Zack Polanski over houseboat council tax | Zack Polanski | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zack Polanski, the Green party leader, is facing scrutiny over his potential failure to pay council tax on a houseboat in London. Anna Turley, chair of the Labour party, has called for an investigation into Polanski's conduct as an elected member of the Greater London authority (GLA). The monitoring officer at the GLA is reviewing the complaint and will decide whether to launch an official investigation.  The Green party maintains that Polanski rented a room elsewhere where council tax was included in the rent and only stayed on the boat occasionally, while Waltham Forest council is investigating potential unpaid council tax for the houseboat's mooring location.

articles.title: Jpmorgan Chase: 'You are worthless': JPMorgan’s Lorna Hajdini faces abusive messages amid legal battle over Chirayu Rana’s 'sex slave' allegations - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lorna Hajdini, a senior executive at JPMorgan Chase, has filed a countersuit against former colleague Chirayu Rana, accusing him of fabricating sexual harassment claims to extort money.  The lawsuit details a series of threatening and abusive emails sent to Hajdini after the legal battle became public, with one email even suggesting she be "gang-raped." JPMorgan Chase has denied Rana's allegations and stated they will not settle the case.

articles.title: Police took independent call on denying permission to CJP event: Parameshwara - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Home Minister G. Parameshwara stated that the police denied permission for a proposed event by the satirical digital outfit, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), after assessing the law and order situation.  The police cited the purpose of the event, participants involved, and related aspects in their decision to deny permission.

articles.title: 'Just a normal Friday for an Iranian': US founder says her wedding in Turkiye got called off - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kiana Ehsani, an Iranian-origin US founder, expressed her heartbreak over the new Green Card rules, which have impacted her personal life.  Ehsani was scheduled to get married in Turkey but had to cancel due to flight cancellations from Iran and family's inability to leave. She highlighted that the new rule forces Iranian visa holders to return home for a green card application, a process she believes is extremely difficult given the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Ehsani emphasized the emotional toll of these restrictions on her and other Iranian individuals in the US.

articles.title: Alain Prost: Formula 1 great injured in masked raid, Swiss media says - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Alain Prost, a former Formula 1 world champion, was injured during a home robbery in Nyon, Switzerland.  Masked individuals entered the home and threatened occupants before slightly injuring one family member and forcing another to open a safe. The incident is under investigation by Swiss and French authorities, who have launched a large-scale search operation. A psychological support team has been provided to the family.

articles.title: A second chance at life: Sangeetha’s brush with a rampaging elephant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sangeetha and her daughter, Shruthi, were both injured when an elephant rammed into their car in Cherur.  The incident occurred as the elephant was on a rampage through the city. The animal lifted the car with its trunk before dropping it back to the ground. Sangeetha described the experience as "nothing short of a second birth" and said she felt like she had gotten her life back, while Shruthi was shaken by the event.

articles.title: 'Hindus and Muslims teaming up to take over Texas': Jan 6 rioter's hate speech at Frisco council meeting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Frisco, Texas council meeting on May 19th saw a former Jan. 6 rioter, Edward Jacob Lang, make inflammatory remarks about India and Muslims, prompting an escort from the meeting.  Lang, a Florida US Senate candidate, also expressed hostility towards mosques and called for their destruction. The meeting focused on approving plans for three places of worship - a mosque, a Hindu temple, and a Jain temple - that have been zoned for religious use for decades.  Mayor Jeff Cheney stated the council's decision was solely based on zoning regulations.

articles.title: Paradeep Singh: Indian-origin worker killed by falling branch in New Zealand, wife left 'completely alone,' without money - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Paradeep Singh, an Indian-origin operations manager, died in Cambridge, New Zealand this week after a falling tree branch struck him while working on his property.  Singh was helping trim branches with others when the incident occurred, leaving behind his newly arrived wife, Kamal. The couple had planned to apply for residency and travel back to India for a wedding celebration. Friends have launched a fundraising campaign to support Kamal and help return Singh's body to India for funeral rites.

articles.title: Aga Khan urges unity, education and service to humanity - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: His Highness Prince Rahim Al Hussaini Aga Khan V, the 50th spiritual leader of the Ismaili community, visited Gilgit-Baltistan on Friday. During his address to a large gathering in Passu, he emphasized the importance of unity, education, and faith within families and communities. Prince Rahim also encouraged young people to prepare for the future with confidence and awareness, urging them to seek global understanding and embrace English language learning. He stressed that Allah's guidance is always present and reminded community members to find peace through prayer and faith.

articles.title: KP announces four Eid holidays from May 26 to 29 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh, and federal governments have announced holidays for Eidul Azha. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government declared four days of holiday from May 26 to May 29, while Sindh also announced a four-day holiday including Friday.  The federal government declared a three-day public holiday from May 26-28. Eidul Azha will be celebrated across Pakistan from May 27 to May 29.

articles.title: ‘You can’t control everything’: the rise in plastic surgeons asked to create ‘AI face’ | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Nora Nugent, president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons, and Dr. Alex Karidis are observing a rise in clients seeking cosmetic surgery based on unrealistic AI-generated images.  These clients often demand procedures that are impossible to achieve through surgery alone, highlighting concerns about the influence of AI on aesthetic ideals and the potential for misleading information.  Surgeons warn against relying solely on these images as they fail to reflect the complexities of human anatomy and healing processes.

articles.title: 'Fast-developing emergency': 1 killed, several injured after fire, explosions at New York City Shipyard - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at a shipyard in New York City on Friday resulted in one fatality and injuries to at least 36 people, including firefighters and first responders. Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore and Chief of Department John Esposito described the incident as a complex emergency with multiple explosions occurring during firefighting efforts. The injured firefighter and fire marshal are currently under medical observation.  The cause of the fire is still under investigation.
